subject: English Language

questions.prompt: Which country has Ngorongoro and Lake Victoria in the script? (A tourism, B Arusha, C Tanzania, D Zanzibar, E Kilimanjaro)
steps: The page 5 script identifies Tanzania. Lake Victoria is shared with neighbouring countries.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How many tourists visited in 2018 according to the script? (A 900, B 900000, C 90, D 9000, E 990)
steps: This answer reproduces the listening text rather than independently verifying tourism statistics.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which place has the highest animal concentration according to the script? (A Serengeti, B Kilimanjaro, C Selous, D Oldonyo Lengai, E Ngorongoro)
steps: The script makes this claim about Serengeti.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest game reserve according to the script? (A Mkomazi, B Ngorongoro, C Serengeti, D Mikumi, E Selous)
steps: The script names Selous.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How much did tourists spend in 2018 according to the script? (A $900, B TSh900000, C $990 million, D $900000 million, E TSh990 million)
steps: Use the script's amount and currency; do not treat it as a verified national total.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. 990 million dollars, as stated in the script.

questions.prompt: Rain fell ___ morning to noon. (A for, B since, C from, D during, E through)
steps: Use from...to for the beginning and end of a period.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I know the man ___ son was bitten. (A whose, B who, C whom, D which, E where)
steps: Whose shows the son's relationship to the man.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Teacher gave us ___ homework that we could not finish. (A little, B many, C few, D much, E more)
steps: Homework is uncountable; so is needed to introduce the degree-result construction.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. Much is intended, but complete grammatical result phrase is so much homework that...

questions.prompt: If I had studied hard, I ___ the assessment. (A pass, B would pass, C would passed, D would have passed, E passed)
steps: A past unreal condition takes would have plus past participle.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Identify quickly in Pupils ran quickly to assembly. (A verb, B adjective, C noun, D conjunction, E adverb)
steps: Quickly describes how they ran.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The patient will die ___ he receives quick treatment. Bank: both, all, if, unless, but, than, neither, then, but also, either.
steps: Unless means if he does not receive treatment.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Father is not only an MP ___ a minister.
steps: Use not only...but also.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: ___ of my eyes hurt.
steps: Both refers to the two eyes.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: He ___ smokes nor drinks.
steps: Use neither...nor.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: No sooner had the bus left ___ we arrived.
steps: Use no sooner...than.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match To be encouraged about something: A campaign, B revenue, C eager, D impressed, E adventure, F commission, G unity.
steps: Impressed means positively affected or admiring; the definition should be corrected.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. Impressed is the closest intended option, but does not exactly mean encouraged.

questions.prompt: Match a group assigned to investigate something.
steps: A commission can be appointed to investigate a matter.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match being ready/keen to do something.
steps: Eager means keen and enthusiastic.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match fighting/working for one goal.
steps: A campaign is organised action to achieve a goal.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match Something that is often an usual (printed).
steps: Adventure describes an unusual or exciting experience, not something merely usual.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E. Adventure is likely intended if unusual experience was meant; no exact match to the printed wording.

questions.prompt: The patient ___ to hospital by neighbours at the moment. (take)
steps: At the moment requires present continuous passive.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Villagers ___ votes last week. (cast)
steps: The past of cast remains cast.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Father ___ to London before the baby was born. (go)
steps: The earlier completed event uses past perfect.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The boy ___ six glasses already. (break)
steps: Already supports present perfect; break has participle broken.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Farmers ___ crops every rainy season. (grow)
steps: A plural habitual subject takes grow.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How many describing characteristics are listed for the station building?
steps: Count the four adjectives in the building-description sentence; broader feature counting needs an explicit rule.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Four: big, beautiful, neat and attractive. The passage also separately mentions a large reception hall and soundproof room.

questions.prompt: What is the condition preventing sound being heard outside a room called?
steps: The passage calls the announcer's room soundproof.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How many seconds did people clap if they clapped for about two minutes?
steps: Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Suggest a suitable title.
steps: Choose a title matching the visit and programme.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Example: Our Visit to Amani Radio Station. Other relevant titles acceptable.

questions.prompt: Give a synonym of opportunity as used in the passage.
steps: Opportunity means a chance to do something.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order A-E: One day he woke in the middle of the night.
steps: This begins the incident after describing the man.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: His friends called him Mr. Forgetful.
steps: This expands the introductory character description.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: He found no cook and no breakfast.
steps: The discovery follows his visit to the kitchen.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Once upon a time there was a forgetful person.
steps: Introduce the character first.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Thinking it morning, he went to the kitchen for breakfast.
steps: His mistaken search follows waking.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Listening: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Grammar and vocabulary: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Grammar: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Comprehension and composition: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: MESP STANDARD SIX ANNUAL EXAMS NOV 2024

limitations: Listening: Geography superlatives and tourism figures are passage claims, not verified national statistics. Ngorongoro is specifically the largest unbroken caldera, rather than every kind of crater.
2(iii): So is omitted from the required so much...that construction.
4(i),4(v): Printed definitions do not accurately match their intended bank answers.
6(i): Four explicitly adjacent building adjectives are counted; additional room features are separately identified.
